transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brings me in is that I just can't seem to keep my mind on a task long enough to actually finish it anymore. Even when it's really important. Like, at work—I'm in computer support—I'll start trying to trace a client's network problem, and ten minutes later I realize I've just reread the exact same log entries three times... and I still have no idea what they even say. It's getting really bad.
Did you struggle with your attention and focus as a child, or is this something that started more recently?

It's definitely been an issue since I was a kid. My mother actually still jokes about my old grade school report cards. She says the teachers always wrote that I was a bright kid, but that I never stayed in my seat, I was always blurting out answers, and... I'd somehow lose my homework even after I had actually finished it. So, yeah, it's not a new problem at all.
Aside from the focus issues, have you been experiencing a persistently low, sad, or depressed mood?

No, I haven't. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, sure, because it's really annoying when I can't just do my job... but I wouldn't say I feel sad or depressed. My mood is actually pretty normal overall.
Do you find yourself struggling with persistent, excessive worry about many different everyday things?
No, not really. I don't spend a lot of time worrying about things. Like I said, I get annoyed when I can't focus on my work, but I'm not sitting around worrying about everything else.
